items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: It must have come out of Nat Toles' band. ... I'd gone, Sir Charles had gone, Henry Coker had gone and the band wasn't really up to par

ctx.x: I think he took that. Really, I don't know. But we called him -- did we call him Sir Charles then? I think we did. It must have come out of Nat Toles' band. And of course, I stayed with that band until I joined Basie in '39 and that's -- that was from Omaha, Nebraska. We had a better band at the time. You know, I've been -- this was miswritten one time. I said one time that when Basie took -- when Basie was -- John Hammond took Basie, bandwise, we were -- we had a better band.

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: And that was the brass. And Sir Charles. Then, of course, you know Charles Christian. He featured and that was it, you know?

ctx.x: And that was the brass. And Sir Charles. Then, of course, you know Charles Christian. He featured and that was it, you know?
